notes:
Quick CRM notes / call snippets:
- Company: Ember Aisle Technologies — multitenant SaaS platform for retail conversational agents (in-store assistant + support bots).
- POC objective: validate Hosted API for prod-like load (50–200 concurrent agent sessions/region), test streaming stability (long lived streams > 8min), and per-tenant quota enforcement + reporting.
- Quote from CTO: "We need streaming to be indistinguishable from real-time — tool calls (inventory lookup, POS actions) must return within SLOs or agents will feel broken."
- AE/SE read: sensitive to 99th percentile latency; willing to start on Hosted to move fast, but will want Dedicated for predictable SLA once load stabilizes.
- Technical ask: websocket streaming reliability, server-side reconnect semantics, KV-cache behavior across model variants, and how Redwood handles tool calling (sync vs async hooks).
- Multi-tenant requirements: per-tenant rate limits, per-tenant usage quotas (monthly token caps), tenant-level logging and billing, ability to throttle or degrade gracefully per tenant.
- Security: SOC2 required, SSO via SAML, KMS integration (customer-managed keys preferred), retention controls for PII, and EU data residency for EMEA tenants.
- Pricing sensitivity: mid-market budget; looking for committed reserved capacity if unit economics are favorable. Wants committed vs burst pricing comparison.
- POC notes: observed intermittent 500s on long streaming sessions when >120 concurrent streams; suspect request routing/worker exhaustion. SE recommended increasing worker pool and enabling prefix/KV caching.
- Ops ask: dashboards for per-tenant token consumption + realtime quota signals (webhooks) to avoid surprises.
- Legal asks: sample DPA and data residency addendum before Dedicated procurement.
- Internal: schedule follow-up with Product/Infra on 2026-03-18 to demo retry/backpressure knobs.
- Sales strategy: push Hosted for MVP fast-path, then justify Dedicated reserved commit after 3-month metrical baseline.
requirements_summary: Workload: chat/agent platform, multi-tenant. Latency targets: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300-350ms (streaming tail preferred). Throughput: 50-200 concurrent agent sessions per region initially, plan to scale to 1k+ after Dedicated. Streaming: must support reconnection with preserved context, tool-calls with sub-500ms roundtrip for external API calls. Quotas: per-tenant rate limits, monthly token caps, realtime quota webhooks and granular billing. Model preferences: open-models acceptable but want verified performance profile; consider quantized variants for cost. Routing/fallback: prefer smart routing to cheaper model for non-critical tenants, automatic fallback to smaller model when Dedicated capacity constrained.
poc_details: 2-week Hosted POC started 2026-03-02. Tests: sustained long-lived streams, tool-calling latency with mocked inventory API, tenant-throttling scenarios. Success metrics: no >1% session drop for 8-min streams, p99 latency <=350ms for streaming tokens, per-tenant rate-limit enforcement within 5s. Current status: early results promising; burst behavior at p99 needs mitigation. SE action: tuning batching + enable KV prefix caching; infra to evaluate worker pool scaling.
commercial_notes: Initial pricing ask: committed 3-node Dedicated equivalent estimate. Want detailed committed vs burst cost model for 12-month term. Consider volume discounts for multi-region deployment. Estimated ARR target once on Dedicated: $120k/year. Legal: needs DPA + data residency addendum. Procurement timeline: evaluation -> procurement in 2026-04 if POC metrics meet thresholds.
risks_and_observations:

- Need clearer pricing for per-tenant quotas; client expects transparent chargebacks.
- Security paperwork in progress; potential delay if KMS/Crypto reviews flag issues.
- Good upsell motion to Dedicated if we can show predictable p99 under tenant churn.
